sanskrit: ākāśagamane śaktiḥ kalāvaidagdhyameva ca | aśrutānāṃ ca śāstrāṇāmabhijñānaṃ vinā gurum || 22 || gamanaṃ sarvalokeṣu prati ghātavivarjitam | atīṃdriyārthadraṣṭṛtvaṃ devaiḥ saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ tathā || 23 || pipīlikādijaṃtūnāṃ vārtājñānamapi dvijāḥ | brahmaviṣṇumahādevalokeṣu gamanaṃ tathā || 24 ||
english: 20b-26. He had perfect knowledge of non-duality characterised by the one-ness of soul. Without study he had the knowledge of the Vedas; he could understand even that which was not heard. O Brāhmaṇas, he had the ability to enter the body of another person, ability to go through the sky, skill in the arts; without a preceptor he could understand the scriptures not heard before. He could go to all the worlds without any obstacle. He could see those objects which are beyond the ken of the sense-organs. He could converse with Devas. He had the knowledge of the activities of ants and other creatures, O Brāhmaṇas. He could travel to the worlds of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Mahādeva. He had the ability to traverse at his will to all the fourteen worlds. These and all other skilful activities usually attributed to Yogins alone, O excellent Brāhmaṇas, Sutīkṣṇa achieved by resorting to Rāmatīrtha.
